sections.title: Action Bar — every setting
sections.summary: The bottom button bar — your primary call-to-action and an optional secondary button. This guide documents every setting of the Action Bar block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

sections.title: Action Bar section
sections.summary: The Action Bar holds the screen's main call-to-action: the primary button (like Continue) and an optional secondary button. This is the control that actually moves visitors forward, so set its label to match what happens next and make sure it points to the same screen you connected on the canvas. It shows on most interactive screens; if a screen has no continuation button, add the next step from the canvas instead.

sections.title: Where it appears
sections.summary: Covered screen types: HeroContent, ListMultiPick, ListSinglePick, GridMultiPick, GridSinglePick, TextInput, WheelPicker, HeroList, WebEmbed.

sections.title: Main button shape and fill
sections.summary: Sets the main button's look — background color, border, corner radius, height, inner padding, and a full-width toggle. For an ad landing page keep it full-width and high-contrast so it reads as the obvious next step. The Visibility toggle hides the button entirely; only hide it when the screen forces a choice first, and never hide both buttons.

sections.title: Motion on the main button
sections.summary: Optional animation for the call-to-action — pulse, glow, bounce, scale, fade-in, slide-up and more, plus an opacity control. A gentle pulse or glow can draw the eye and lift taps; save attention-grabbing effects for your key conversion screen and avoid stacking several. Leave it off for a calm, professional feel.

sections.title: Gradient on the main button
sections.summary: An optional color gradient layered over the button's solid fill — set start and end colors, the angle, extra color stops, and an optional moving shimmer. Leave it off for a clean flat look; turn it on to make the call-to-action pop against a busy background. Keep enough contrast that the label stays easy to read.

sections.title: Icon on the main button
sections.summary: An optional icon next to the label — choose start or end placement, size, corner radius, and spacing, and how it fits its box (fit shows the whole icon, fill crops to cover). A small leading arrow or lock icon can reinforce the action; keep it in the same color family as the label. Leave it empty for a clean text-only button.

sections.title: Main button label
sections.summary: The text on your main call-to-action button — the one that moves visitors to the next screen. Make it a short, specific verb phrase tied to the action (Continue, Get my plan, Subscribe) rather than a generic word; clear, benefit-led labels lift click-through on a paid landing page. This text can be translated per language.

sections.title: Shadow under the main button
sections.summary: An optional drop shadow beneath the button, with control over its color, blur, and vertical drop. A soft shadow lifts the call-to-action off the page so it feels tappable; keep it subtle (low blur, small offset) so it looks intentional rather than heavy. Leave it off if your theme is flat.

sections.title: Main button text style
sections.summary: Typography for the main button label — font, weight, size, color, and alignment. Leave it on the theme defaults for a consistent look; bump the weight or size, or switch color, only when the label is hard to read against the button fill. Applies to the label in every language.

sections.title: Secondary button shape and fill
sections.summary: Sets the secondary button's look — background, border, corner radius, height, padding, and a full-width toggle. Give it lower visual weight than the main button (an outline or transparent fill works well) so it doesn't compete with your call-to-action. The Visibility toggle hides it; never hide both the primary and secondary buttons.

sections.title: Motion on the secondary button
sections.summary: Adds optional movement to the secondary (lower-priority) button, such as pulse, glow, or bounce, plus an opacity control to fade it. Leave this off by default. Animation draws the eye, so reserve it for your main button only; making the alternative path move competes with your primary call to action and typically lowers conversions.

sections.title: Gradient on the secondary button
sections.summary: An optional color gradient over the secondary button's solid fill (start/end colors, angle, stops, optional shimmer). Usually leave this off — a gradient draws attention, which you want on your main call-to-action, not the side path. Turn it on only if a flat secondary clashes with your theme.

sections.title: Icon on the secondary button
sections.summary: An optional icon on the secondary button — placement (start or end), size, corner radius, spacing, and how it fits its box (fit shows the whole icon, fill crops to cover). Usually leave it empty so the secondary stays understated; add one only when it clarifies the action, like a back arrow for Go back.

sections.title: Secondary button label
sections.summary: Text for the optional second button — use it for a side path like Skip, Maybe later, or Restore purchase, never your main goal. On funnel steps an easy escape route can cost conversions, so leave it empty unless you genuinely need the alternative; on a paywall a low-key secondary is fine.

sections.title: Shadow under the secondary button
sections.summary: An optional drop shadow under the secondary button (color, blur, vertical drop). Keep it lighter than the main button's shadow, or off entirely, so the secondary stays visually subordinate to your call-to-action.

sections.title: Secondary button text style
sections.summary: Typography for the secondary button label — font, weight, size, color, and alignment. Style it deliberately quieter than the main button (lighter weight, muted color) so your primary call-to-action stays the obvious choice. Leave it on theme defaults unless the hierarchy looks off.

sections.title: • Background color
sections.summary: The button fill color.

sections.title: • Border color
sections.summary: Color of that outline.

sections.title: • Border width
sections.summary: Thickness (px) of the button outline; 0 hides it.

sections.title: • Button height
sections.summary: Fixed height of the button in pixels. Keep it tap-friendly (≈44px or taller).

sections.title: • Button padding
sections.summary: Inner spacing between the label/icon and the button edges (top, right, bottom, left).

sections.title: • Corner radius
sections.summary: How rounded the button corners are (px); higher is softer.

sections.title: • Full width
sections.summary: Stretch the button across the whole bar. Full-width reads as the obvious next step on a phone; turn it off for a button only as wide as its label.

sections.title: • Visibility
sections.summary: Show or hide this button entirely. Never hide both buttons, or the screen has no way forward.

sections.title: • Width
sections.summary: Explicit button width — used when Full width is off.

sections.title: Motion on the main button
sections.summary: Optional animation for the call-to-action — pulse, glow, bounce, scale, fade-in, slide-up and more, plus an opacity control. A gentle pulse or glow can draw the eye and lift taps; save attention-grabbing effects for your key conversion screen and avoid stacking several. Leave it off for a calm, professional feel.

sections.title: Motion on the main button
sections.summary: Motion on the main button

sections.title: • Animation
sections.summary: An optional looping motion to draw the eye to the action — choose from None, Pulse, Shimmer, Bounce, Shake, Glow, Ripple, Scale, Fade In, Slide Up or Wiggle.

sections.title: • Enable effects
sections.summary: Off by default (gated on opacity). Turning it on sets the button to full opacity and a default Shimmer animation, then reveals the opacity slider and animation menu. (The animation choice is remembered but inactive while effects are off.)

sections.title: • Opacity
sections.summary: How see-through the whole button is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid).

sections.title: Gradient on the main button
sections.summary: An optional color gradient layered over the button's solid fill — set start and end colors, the angle, extra color stops, and an optional moving shimmer. Leave it off for a clean flat look; turn it on to make the call-to-action pop against a busy background. Keep enough contrast that the label stays easy to read.

sections.title: Gradient on the main button
sections.summary: Gradient on the main button

sections.title: • Angle / direction
sections.summary: Which way the colors flow across the button. Medium offers preset directions (e.g. 90° left→right, 180° top→bottom); Advanced lets you type any angle from 0–360°.

sections.title: • Color stops (Advanced)
sections.summary: The full list of colors in the gradient. Add up to five stops and set each stop’s color and its position (0–100%) along the sweep, for multi-color blends beyond a simple two-color fade.

sections.title: • Detail level
sections.summary: A complexity switch (not saved on its own): Simple = just a start and end color; Medium = adds a direction angle and a shimmer toggle; Advanced = multi-stop colors plus a numeric angle, size and the full shimmer controls. Pick the depth you need.

sections.title: • Enable gradient
sections.summary: Off by default — the button uses a single flat color. Turn this on to blend colors across the fill for a richer look; turn it off for a clean solid button.

sections.title: • End color
sections.summary: The color the gradient fades to (the last color stop). Keep enough contrast with the start color that the label stays readable.

sections.title: • Gradient size (Advanced)
sections.summary: How far the gradient is stretched, from 50% (tight, punchy transition) to 200% (soft, gradual spread).

sections.title: • Shimmer
sections.summary: An optional animated sheen that sweeps across the button. When on you can tune the trigger (on hover, on a timer, or off), the streak color, its width and skew (slant), the duration of one sweep, and — for the timer trigger — the cycle gap between sweeps.

sections.title: • Start color
sections.summary: The color the gradient begins with (the first color stop / left-most stop in Advanced).

sections.title: Icon on the main button
sections.summary: An optional icon next to the label — choose start or end placement, size, corner radius, and spacing, and how it fits its box (fit shows the whole icon, fill crops to cover). A small leading arrow or lock icon can reinforce the action; keep it in the same color family as the label. Leave it empty for a clean text-only button.

sections.title: Icon on the main button
sections.summary: Icon on the main button

sections.title: • Corner radius
sections.summary: Rounding of the icon’s corners in pixels; raise it to clip a square image into a rounded or circular badge.

sections.title: • Enable icon
sections.summary: Off by default. Turn on to show an image (icon) alongside the button label; off for a text-only button.

sections.title: • Height
sections.summary: The icon’s height in pixels (0–200).

sections.title: • Icon image
sections.summary: Upload an image file or paste an image URL — the icon shown next to the label. Leave empty to show no graphic.

sections.title: • Icon padding
sections.summary: The space around the icon (top, right, bottom, left) — the gap between the icon and the label and the button edges.

sections.title: • Placement
sections.summary: Where the icon sits relative to the label: Start (before the text) or End (after it); the Fixed Start/End variants pin it to the button’s left/right edge; Top and Bottom stack it above or below the label.

sections.title: • Scale mode
sections.summary: How the image fits its box: Scale to Fill (stretch), Aspect Fit (show the whole icon, may letterbox), Aspect Fill (cover the box, may crop), or Center (no resize).

sections.title: • Width
sections.summary: The icon’s width in pixels (0–200).

subarticles.title: • Background color
subarticles.summary: The button fill color.

subarticles.title: • Border color
subarticles.summary: Color of that outline.

subarticles.title: • Border width
subarticles.summary: Thickness (px) of the button outline; 0 hides it.

subarticles.title: • Button height
subarticles.summary: Fixed height of the button in pixels. Keep it tap-friendly (≈44px or taller).

subarticles.title: • Button padding
subarticles.summary: Inner spacing between the label/icon and the button edges (top, right, bottom, left).

subarticles.title: • Corner radius
subarticles.summary: How rounded the button corners are (px); higher is softer.

subarticles.title: • Full width
subarticles.summary: Stretch the button across the whole bar. Full-width reads as the obvious next step on a phone; turn it off for a button only as wide as its label.

subarticles.title: • Visibility
subarticles.summary: Show or hide this button entirely. Never hide both buttons, or the screen has no way forward.

subarticles.title: • Width
subarticles.summary: Explicit button width — used when Full width is off.

subarticles.title: Motion on the main button
subarticles.summary: Optional animation for the call-to-action — pulse, glow, bounce, scale, fade-in, slide-up and more, plus an opacity control. A gentle pulse or glow can draw the eye and lift taps; save attention-grabbing effects for your key conversion screen and avoid stacking several. Leave it off for a calm, professional feel.

subarticles.title: Motion on the main button
subarticles.summary: Motion on the main button

subarticles.title: • Animation
subarticles.summary: An optional looping motion to draw the eye to the action — choose from None, Pulse, Shimmer, Bounce, Shake, Glow, Ripple, Scale, Fade In, Slide Up or Wiggle.

subarticles.title: • Enable effects
subarticles.summary: Off by default (gated on opacity). Turning it on sets the button to full opacity and a default Shimmer animation, then reveals the opacity slider and animation menu. (The animation choice is remembered but inactive while effects are off.)

subarticles.title: • Opacity
subarticles.summary: How see-through the whole button is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid).

subarticles.title: Gradient on the main button
subarticles.summary: An optional color gradient layered over the button's solid fill — set start and end colors, the angle, extra color stops, and an optional moving shimmer. Leave it off for a clean flat look; turn it on to make the call-to-action pop against a busy background. Keep enough contrast that the label stays easy to read.

subarticles.title: Gradient on the main button
subarticles.summary: Gradient on the main button

subarticles.title: • Angle / direction
subarticles.summary: Which way the colors flow across the button. Medium offers preset directions (e.g. 90° left→right, 180° top→bottom); Advanced lets you type any angle from 0–360°.

subarticles.title: • Color stops (Advanced)
subarticles.summary: The full list of colors in the gradient. Add up to five stops and set each stop’s color and its position (0–100%) along the sweep, for multi-color blends beyond a simple two-color fade.

subarticles.title: • Detail level
subarticles.summary: A complexity switch (not saved on its own): Simple = just a start and end color; Medium = adds a direction angle and a shimmer toggle; Advanced = multi-stop colors plus a numeric angle, size and the full shimmer controls. Pick the depth you need.

subarticles.title: • Enable gradient
subarticles.summary: Off by default — the button uses a single flat color. Turn this on to blend colors across the fill for a richer look; turn it off for a clean solid button.

subarticles.title: • End color
subarticles.summary: The color the gradient fades to (the last color stop). Keep enough contrast with the start color that the label stays readable.

subarticles.title: • Gradient size (Advanced)
subarticles.summary: How far the gradient is stretched, from 50% (tight, punchy transition) to 200% (soft, gradual spread).

subarticles.title: • Shimmer
subarticles.summary: An optional animated sheen that sweeps across the button. When on you can tune the trigger (on hover, on a timer, or off), the streak color, its width and skew (slant), the duration of one sweep, and — for the timer trigger — the cycle gap between sweeps.

subarticles.title: • Start color
subarticles.summary: The color the gradient begins with (the first color stop / left-most stop in Advanced).

subarticles.title: Icon on the main button
subarticles.summary: An optional icon next to the label — choose start or end placement, size, corner radius, and spacing, and how it fits its box (fit shows the whole icon, fill crops to cover). A small leading arrow or lock icon can reinforce the action; keep it in the same color family as the label. Leave it empty for a clean text-only button.

subarticles.title: Icon on the main button
subarticles.summary: Icon on the main button

subarticles.title: • Corner radius
subarticles.summary: Rounding of the icon’s corners in pixels; raise it to clip a square image into a rounded or circular badge.

subarticles.title: • Enable icon
subarticles.summary: Off by default. Turn on to show an image (icon) alongside the button label; off for a text-only button.

subarticles.title: • Height
subarticles.summary: The icon’s height in pixels (0–200).

subarticles.title: • Icon image
subarticles.summary: Upload an image file or paste an image URL — the icon shown next to the label. Leave empty to show no graphic.

subarticles.title: • Icon padding
subarticles.summary: The space around the icon (top, right, bottom, left) — the gap between the icon and the label and the button edges.

subarticles.title: • Placement
subarticles.summary: Where the icon sits relative to the label: Start (before the text) or End (after it); the Fixed Start/End variants pin it to the button’s left/right edge; Top and Bottom stack it above or below the label.

subarticles.title: • Scale mode
subarticles.summary: How the image fits its box: Scale to Fill (stretch), Aspect Fit (show the whole icon, may letterbox), Aspect Fill (cover the box, may crop), or Center (no resize).

subarticles.title: • Width
subarticles.summary: The icon’s width in pixels (0–200).

subarticles.title: Main button label
subarticles.summary: Main button label

subarticles.title: Shadow under the main button
subarticles.summary: An optional drop shadow beneath the button, with control over its color, blur, and vertical drop. A soft shadow lifts the call-to-action off the page so it feels tappable; keep it subtle (low blur, small offset) so it looks intentional rather than heavy. Leave it off if your theme is flat.

subarticles.title: Shadow under the main button
subarticles.summary: Shadow under the main button

subarticles.title: • Blur
subarticles.summary: How soft and spread-out the shadow is, from 0 (hard edge) to 50 (very diffuse).

subarticles.title: • Color
subarticles.summary: The shadow color, including its transparency (default is a semi-transparent black). A tinted, low-opacity color gives a subtle lift.

subarticles.title: • Enable shadow
subarticles.summary: Off by default. Turn on to cast a soft drop shadow beneath the button so it lifts off the background; off keeps it flat.

subarticles.title: • Vertical offset
subarticles.summary: How far the shadow sits below (positive) or above (negative) the button, −50 to 50 px.

subarticles.title: Main button text style
subarticles.summary: Typography for the main button label — font, weight, size, color, and alignment. Leave it on the theme defaults for a consistent look; bump the weight or size, or switch color, only when the label is hard to read against the button fill. Applies to the label in every language.

subarticles.title: Main button text style
subarticles.summary: Main button text style

subarticles.summary: Fill drawn behind the label text (a highlight pill).

subarticles.summary: Transparency of the label background (0–100%).

subarticles.title: • Background radius
subarticles.summary: Corner rounding of the label background.

subarticles.title: • Font family
subarticles.summary: Typeface of the button label.

subarticles.title: • Font size
subarticles.summary: Text size (px) of the label.

subarticles.title: • Font weight
subarticles.summary: How bold the label is.

subarticles.title: • Line height
subarticles.summary: Vertical spacing of the label text.

subarticles.title: • Strikethrough color
subarticles.summary: Color of a line-through decoration when used (for example, an old price).

subarticles.title: • Text align
subarticles.summary: Alignment of the label within the button.

subarticles.title: • Text color
subarticles.summary: Color of the label text.

subarticles.title: Secondary button label
subarticles.summary: Text for the optional second button — use it for a side path like Skip, Maybe later, or Restore purchase, never your main goal. The Visibility toggle hides it; never hide both the primary and secondary buttons.

translations.en: The space around the icon (top, right, bottom, left) — the gap between the icon and the label and the button edges.

nodes.label: Group: Secondary button
Secondary button in the section

en.name: Where the Secondary button sits inside the open Action Bar section.

nodes.label: Element caption

translations.en: Inside the Action Bar section, this is the Secondary button.

nodes.label: Secondary button · Secondary button label

translations.en: Text for the optional second button — use it for a side path like Skip, Maybe later, or Restore purchase, never your main goal. On funnel steps an easy escape route can cost conversions, so leave it empty unless you genuinely need the alternative; on a paywall a low-key secondary is fine.

nodes.label: Secondary button label

en.name: Where to find “Secondary button label” in the editor.

nodes.label: Secondary button · Secondary button text style

translations.en: Typography for the secondary button label — font, weight, size, color, and alignment. Style it deliberately quieter than the main button (lighter weight, muted color) so your primary call-to-action stays the obvious choice. Leave it on theme defaults unless the hierarchy looks off.

nodes.label: Secondary button text style

en.name: Where to find “Secondary button text style” in the editor.

nodes.label: Secondary button text style · Background color

translations.en: Fill drawn behind the label text (a highlight pill).

nodes.label: Secondary button text style · Font family
Secondary button text style · Line height

translations.en: Vertical spacing of the label text.

nodes.label: Secondary button text style · Font size
Secondary button text style · Font weight
Secondary button text style · Text color
Secondary button text style · Text align

translations.en: Alignment of the label within the button.

nodes.label: Secondary button text style · Strikethrough color

translations.en: Color of a line-through decoration when used (for example, an old price).

nodes.label: Secondary button text style · Background opacity
Secondary button text style · Background radius

translations.en: Corner rounding of the label background.

nodes.label: Secondary button · Secondary button shape and fill

translations.en: Sets the secondary button's look — background, border, corner radius, height, padding, and a full-width toggle. Give it lower visual weight than the main button (an outline or transparent fill works well) so it doesn't compete with your call-to-action. The Visibility toggle hides it; never hide both the primary and secondary buttons.

nodes.label: Secondary button shape and fill

en.name: Where to find “Secondary button shape and fill” in the editor.

nodes.label: Secondary button shape and fill · Visibility

translations.en: Show or hide this button entirely. Never hide both buttons, or the screen has no way forward.

nodes.label: Secondary button shape and fill · Full width

translations.en: Stretch the button across the whole bar. Full-width reads as the obvious next step on a phone; turn it off for a button only as wide as its label.

nodes.label: Secondary button shape and fill · Button height

translations.en: Fixed height of the button in pixels. Keep it tap-friendly (≈44px or taller).

nodes.label: Secondary button shape and fill · Background color
Secondary button shape and fill · Border width

translations.en: Thickness (px) of the button outline; 0 hides it.

nodes.label: Secondary button shape and fill · Border color
Secondary button shape and fill · Corner radius

translations.en: How rounded the button corners are (px); higher is softer.

nodes.label: Secondary button shape and fill · Width

translations.en: Explicit button width — used when Full width is off.

nodes.label: Secondary button shape and fill · Button padding

translations.en: Inner spacing between the label/icon and the button edges (top, right, bottom, left).

nodes.label: Secondary button · Gradient on the secondary button

translations.en: An optional color gradient over the secondary button's solid fill (start/end colors, angle, stops, optional shimmer). Usually leave this off — a gradient draws attention, which you want on your main call-to-action, not the side path. Turn it on only if a flat secondary clashes with your theme.

nodes.label: Gradient on the secondary button

en.name: Where to find “Gradient on the secondary button” in the editor.

nodes.label: Gradient on the secondary button · Enable gradient

translations.en: Off by default — the button uses a single flat color. Turn this on to blend colors across the fill for a richer look; turn it off for a clean solid button.

nodes.label: Gradient on the secondary button · Detail level

translations.en: A complexity switch (not saved on its own): Simple = just a start and end color; Medium = adds a direction angle and a shimmer toggle; Advanced = multi-stop colors plus a numeric angle, size and the full shimmer controls. Pick the depth you need.

nodes.label: Gradient on the secondary button · Start color

translations.en: The color the gradient begins with (the first color stop / left-most stop in Advanced).

nodes.label: Gradient on the secondary button · End color

translations.en: The color the gradient fades to (the last color stop). Keep enough contrast with the start color that the label stays readable.

nodes.label: Gradient on the secondary button · Angle / direction

translations.en: Which way the colors flow across the button. Medium offers preset directions (e.g. 90° left→right, 180° top→bottom); Advanced lets you type any angle from 0–360°.

nodes.label: Gradient on the secondary button · Color stops (Advanced)

translations.en: The full list of colors in the gradient. Add up to five stops and set each stop’s color and its position (0–100%) along the sweep, for multi-color blends beyond a simple two-color fade.

nodes.label: Gradient on the secondary button · Gradient size (Advanced)

translations.en: How far the gradient is stretched, from 50% (tight, punchy transition) to 200% (soft, gradual spread).

nodes.label: Gradient on the secondary button · Shimmer

translations.en: An optional animated sheen that sweeps across the button. When on you can tune the trigger (on hover, on a timer, or off), the streak color, its width and skew (slant), the duration of one sweep, and — for the timer trigger — the cycle gap between sweeps.

nodes.label: Secondary button · Shadow under the secondary button

translations.en: An optional drop shadow under the secondary button (color, blur, vertical drop). Keep it lighter than the main button's shadow, or off entirely, so the secondary stays visually subordinate to your call-to-action.

nodes.label: Shadow under the secondary button

en.name: Where to find “Shadow under the secondary button” in the editor.

nodes.label: Shadow under the secondary button · Enable shadow

translations.en: Off by default. Turn on to cast a soft drop shadow beneath the button so it lifts off the background; off keeps it flat.

nodes.label: Shadow under the secondary button · Color

translations.en: The shadow color, including its transparency (default is a semi-transparent black). A tinted, low-opacity color gives a subtle lift.

nodes.label: Shadow under the secondary button · Blur

translations.en: How soft and spread-out the shadow is, from 0 (hard edge) to 50 (very diffuse).

nodes.label: Shadow under the secondary button · Vertical offset

translations.en: How far the shadow sits below (positive) or above (negative) the button, −50 to 50 px.

nodes.label: Secondary button · Motion on the secondary button

translations.en: Adds optional movement to the secondary (lower-priority) button, such as pulse, glow, or bounce, plus an opacity control to fade it. Leave this off by default. Animation draws the eye, so reserve it for your main button only; making the alternative path move competes with your primary call to action and typically lowers conversions.

nodes.label: Motion on the secondary button

en.name: Where to find “Motion on the secondary button” in the editor.

nodes.label: Motion on the secondary button · Enable effects

translations.en: Off by default (gated on opacity). Turning it on sets the button to full opacity and a default Shimmer animation, then reveals the opacity slider and animation menu. (The animation choice is remembered but inactive while effects are off.)

nodes.label: Motion on the secondary button · Opacity

translations.en: How see-through the whole button is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid).

nodes.label: Motion on the secondary button · Animation

translations.en: An optional looping motion to draw the eye to the action — choose from None, Pulse, Shimmer, Bounce, Shake, Glow, Ripple, Scale, Fade In, Slide Up or Wiggle.

nodes.label: Secondary button · Icon on the secondary button

translations.en: An optional icon on the secondary button — placement (start or end), size, corner radius, spacing, and how it fits its box (fit shows the whole icon, fill crops to cover). Usually leave it empty so the secondary stays understated; add one only when it clarifies the action, like a back arrow for Go back.

nodes.label: Icon on the secondary button

en.name: Where to find “Icon on the secondary button” in the editor.

nodes.label: Icon on the secondary button · Enable icon

translations.en: Off by default. Turn on to show an image (icon) alongside the button label; off for a text-only button.

nodes.label: Icon on the secondary button · Icon image

translations.en: Upload an image file or paste an image URL — the icon shown next to the label. Leave empty to show no graphic.

nodes.label: Icon on the secondary button · Placement

translations.en: Where the icon sits relative to the label: Start (before the text) or End (after it); the Fixed Start/End variants pin it to the button’s left/right edge; Top and Bottom stack it above or below the label.

nodes.label: Icon on the secondary button · Scale mode

translations.en: How the image fits its box: Scale to Fill (stretch), Aspect Fit (show the whole icon, may letterbox), Aspect Fill (cover the box, may crop), or Center (no resize).

nodes.label: Icon on the secondary button · Width
Icon on the secondary button · Height
Icon on the secondary button · Corner radius

translations.en: Rounding of the icon’s corners in pixels; raise it to clip a square image into a rounded or circular badge.

nodes.label: Icon on the secondary button · Icon padding

translations.en: The space around the icon (top, right, bottom, left) — the gap between the icon and the label and the button edges.
